shortDescription: By Dietrich KnauthArizona Attorney General Kris Mayes on Wednesday sued drink maker Botanic Tonics LLC, saying the company illegally sold kratom and kava tonics as "energy drinks" without disclosing the products' risks of addiction and withdrawal.

children: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes on Wednesday sued drink maker Botanic Tonics LLC, saying the company illegally sold kratom and kava tonics as "energy drinks" without disclosing the products' risks of addiction and withdrawal.
Botanic Tonics sells drinks under the "Feel free" brand in Arizona, and it is marketed as a wellness tonic, energy drink and a healthier alternative to alcohol.
"Feel free" contains the psychoactive substance kratom, which has opioid-like qualities and is known colloquially as "gas station heroin," according to the lawsuit.
Botanic Tonics markets the drinks to youth and its advertising obscures the drinks' kratom content, according to the lawsuit.
Botanic Tonics did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Arizona had 146 kratom-related deaths from 2020 to 2023, according to the attorney general.
Kratom is legal under federal law, but the US Drug Enforcement Administration moved to restrict higher-concentration kratom products earlier this year.
Texas, Missouri and the city of Baltimore have also filed lawsuits against companies that sell kratom products.
